touches.text: Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.

A trouble has a point of origin, and that is how they match: when raised, its emission source AND error message are checked against the open tickets. If found, increment; either way, pass the ticket back to the caller.
Disposable once closed. File artifacts in the logging tree, cleared on the 30 day cycle by the cairn device during sleep (4.3.2.4).
Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.

A proof MAY read the live database; what a test writes stays out of live, either in the TESTING database or marked as a testing artifact that the rest of the system ignores (Akien, Q#112, 2026-11-14: "we want as much of the system as possible to be able to igore testing artifactd. i see no reason why a proof can't read a live db, might mean not having to populate test data."). WHY: reading live saves populating test data; ignoring testing artifacts keeps them from leaking into what the system believes. This agrees with his 2026-09-28 rule: test against live, marked as testing. -amm
Messages sit in a SMALL buffer in memory. WHY: in memory is faster.

A message nobody picks up within n milliseconds is pushed out of the buffer to the database, into a table that is just a table of messages. That table is the bus's exception to the memory model (4.3.1.5): it is not learning, and the buffer in front of it is what keeps the bus fast.
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).

Its web panel is the operator's to-do list: email, trouble tickets, open questions (the ones only the operator can answer). The list is live: items appear as they arrive and leave as they're answered or resolved.
